memo_delta.stage_one_comment: Emaar stays on the Watchlist because the evidence still does not clear the original entry gates. The issuer’s half-year release shows slower backlog growth, below the threshold in the July thesis, while recognized revenue and EBITDA grew. That combination matters: the leading demand signal can weaken even while past sales support reported profit. It does not justify calling the entire earnings base a collapse. We could not verify standalone second-quarter pre-sales growth or the profit result against the original consensus from this release, so those forecasts remain unassessable at this checkpoint. The shares are below the stale original reference price, but no Watchlist position was taken and matched benchmark returns are missing. Price weakness therefore does not earn a skill verdict. Continue watching quarterly demand, owner actions, funding and the upcoming dividend window. The longer forecasts remain open, no current confidence number is manufactured, and the published thesis and prior review are preserved.
